introduction_markdown:
**General Certificate of Education Board - General Certificate of Education Examination. Physics 2 (0780), ADVANCED LEVEL, June 2023. Time allowed: three hours.**

Answer ALL questions. Section I is designed to be answered in 1 hour, Section II in 30 minutes and Section III in 1 hour. You are advised to divide your time accordingly. You are reminded of the necessity for good English and orderly presentation in your answers. In calculations you must show all the steps in your working, giving your answer at each stage. Calculators and formulae booklet are allowed.

**Structure of the paper.** SECTION I (headed "One hour 30 minutes" on page 2): questions 1 to 5 are compulsory; in question 6 answer EITHER 6 (a), (b) and (c) OR 6 (d), (e) and (f). SECTION II (40 minutes): DATA ANALYSIS, question 7. SECTION III (50 minutes): OPTIONS - answer any two questions from the four options (Option 1: Energy resources and environmental physics, question 8; Option 2: Communication, question 9; Option 3: Electronics, question 10; Option 4: Medical physics, question 11).

No data sheet is printed in the paper: whenever a constant is needed, the model answer states the value it uses.
enonce_intro_markdown: The volume of a gas changes from $1.80\times10^{-6}\,\mathrm{m^3}$ to $3.20\times10^{-3}\,\mathrm{m^3}$ as it expands adiabatically against the atmosphere which exerts a pressure of $1.10\times10^{5}\,\mathrm{Pa}$.
incertitudes: Question 2 : aucune constante nécessaire. Le travail vaut 352 J avec ou sans le volume initial (1,80e-6 m3 négligeable devant 3,20e-3 m3).

questions.enonce_markdown: Calculate the total work done by the gas.
questions.corrige_markdown:
The gas expands against a constant external pressure, so the work done by the gas is

$$W = p\,\Delta V = p\,(V_2 - V_1)$$

$$\Delta V = 3.20\times10^{-3} - 1.80\times10^{-6} = 3.1982\times10^{-3}\ \mathrm{m^3}$$

$$W = 1.10\times10^{5}\times 3.1982\times10^{-3} = 351.8\ \mathrm{J}$$

**Work done by the gas $\approx 3.52\times10^{2}\ \mathrm{J}$.** (The initial volume is only 0.06 % of the final volume, so ignoring it gives the same value to 3 significant figures.)

questions.enonce_markdown:
(i) State and explain how the temperature of the gas changes in the process.

(ii) Name one practical situation in which this change can be experienced.
questions.corrige_markdown:
(i) **The temperature of the gas falls.**

The expansion is adiabatic, so no heat is exchanged with the surroundings: $Q = 0$. By the first law of thermodynamics, $\Delta U = Q - W$, where $W$ is the work done **by** the gas. Hence $\Delta U = -W = -352\ \mathrm{J}$: the internal energy of the gas decreases. For a gas, the internal energy is the total kinetic energy of the random motion of its molecules (and for an ideal gas it depends only on temperature), so a decrease in internal energy means a decrease in the mean kinetic energy of the molecules, that is, a fall in temperature. The gas does work on the atmosphere at the expense of its own internal energy.

(ii) Examples: the air rushing out of a burst or deflating tyre (or the gas escaping from an aerosol can or a carbon dioxide fire extinguisher) feels cold, because the gas expands rapidly, too fast for heat to flow in, and cools.
